title: Annotatio I §.IV IMPLICITE Lutheran: Flacius’s complexum / duplex mass — both readings tropical
pass_a_gloss: The other is Flacius Illyricus’s: This complex, or this mass consisting of two things, is my body; of which both [readings] are most openly tropical — the former metonymic, of Container for contained; the latter synecdochic, of Part for whole.
pass_b_english: Flacius Illyricus’s other reading: This complex / this mass of two things is my body.
Both readings are openly tropical — Luther’s as metonymy of container for contained; Flacius’s as synecdoche of part for whole.
source_text: Altera Flacii Illyrici: Hoc complexum, seu haec massa ex duabus rebus constans, est corpus meum; quorum utraque apertissimè tropica; prior metonymica, Continentis pro contento, posterior synechdochica, Partis pro toto.

lemmas.gloss: this complex / mass of two things
